title: KV reservation quotas and deferred soft-eviction policy for paged-attention workloads
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Problem: Paged attention combined with multi-tenant KV caches creates frequent micro-evictions and fragmentation. Short-lived evictions (hard reclaim) cause decode prefill misses and transient 95th/99th percentile token latency spikes for high-concurrency workloads. Current eviction is reactive and global: when a shard hits capacity we evict best-effort, causing noisy neighbor effects and suboptimal kernel selection (sparse fragments force slower kernels).

Proposal: implement a two-part system: 1) per-tenant/shard reservation quotas (token/page reservations) that guarantee a minimal KV working set during prefill/decode, and 2) a deferred/soft-eviction policy that prefers graceful reclamation windows and consolidation rather than immediate hard reclamation. The system will include an eviction scoring function that factors recent access heat, affinity to current kernels, fragmentation cost (estimated kernel slow-down if fragmented), and tail-latency risk. A background consolidator will run opportunistically to coalesce small fragments into dense segments to enable fast kernels. Reservation and soft-eviction are configurable per-customer and exposed to the autoscaling and kernel-selection layers.

Goals: reduce 95th and 99th token decode latency spikes caused by KV churn; reduce average kernel slow-path invocations due to fragmentation; provide fair multi-tenant behavior under contention; keep throughput and average latency regressions <= 2% vs baseline.
acceptance_criteria: 95th-token decode latency for our multi-tenant bench (200 concurrently active streams) is reduced by >=20% vs baseline under the same memory budget
Rate of hard-eviction events per minute on overloaded shards is reduced by >=60% during experimental workload
No throughput regression >2% across latency-optimized and throughput-optimized kernels
Feature is behind config flags and can be toggled at route/shard granularity
Unit tests for reservation allocator, eviction scorer, and background consolidator exist
Integration tests validate kernel hinting when consolidation completes (simulated dense segment)
tasks: Write design doc describing reservation token model, API surface and config (owner: Diego)
Add reservation allocator to KV manager with per-shard accounting and LRU fallbacks
Implement soft-eviction scorer: heat, recency, kernel-fragment-penalty, tenant-priority weighting
Background consolidator process that runs with backoff and respects GPU utilization windows
Kernel hint API: expose segment density score so scheduler picks fast kernels when available
E2E perf harness and benchmark job: multi-tenant replay including synthetic fragmentation pattern
Add feature flags and runtime knobs for reservation sizes, defer window, consolidation thresholds
Write unit and integration tests; QA run and perf analysis
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Reservations could starve bursts and reduce cache efficiency; Mitigation: soft quotas with reclaimable emergency pool and short lease TTLs
Risk: Consolidator adds GPU/CPU overhead; Mitigation: run during low-util windows and throttle based on util signals
Risk: Incorrect scorer weights lead to oscillations; Mitigation: staged rollout with telemetry and adaptive dampening
Risk: Multi-tenant fairness edges; Mitigation: allow per-tenant priority and promote isolation via Dedicated tiers
metrics_and_observability: Per-shard reserved vs used pages over time
Hard-eviction events per shard and per-tenant
Fragmentation ratio (num_fragments / pages) and average fragment size
Kernel slow-path invocation rate attributed to fragmented segments
95th/99th token decode latency annotated with eviction events
Consolidation CPU/GPU time and reclaimed bytes
testing_plan: Unit tests for allocator correctness, race-free accounting and TTL expirations
Microbench: synthetic workload with rapid ephemeral contexts to validate reduced hard-evictions
Multi-tenant replay job using production traces with added synthetic fragmentation phases
A/B rollout in staging: 50% routes with feature enabled; collect latencies and kernel selection histograms
Chaos experiments: force background consolidator to fail and ensure graceful fallback to hard-eviction
